# Saudi Huroob (Absconding) 2026: Check, Remove or Transfer

Saudi huroob and absconding guide for 2026. Check absent-from-work status, understand the 60-day Qiwa period, transfer or final exit options, false reports and domestic worker rules.

[Editorial policy](/editorial-policy)

In everyday expat language, **huroob** or an **absconding case** usually means that a worker has an absence-related status in Saudi labour or residency records. Saudi official systems now more commonly use terms such as **work discontinuation** and **absent from work**.

For many private-sector Qiwa cases, the important period is **60 days**. During that period, an eligible worker may be able to transfer legally to a new employer or complete final exit. If no permitted action is completed, the status can become **absent from work**, and the normal transfer or final-exit route can become harder.

There is no single button that removes every huroob case. The correct solution depends on the exact Qiwa status, report or action date, contract history, whether the worker is inside Saudi Arabia, whether the case is false, and whether a current status-correction route is available.

## [Quick Answer](#quick-answer)

| Question | Practical Answer |
|----|----|
| What is huroob in Saudi Arabia? | Huroob is a common expat word for an absence or absconding-related labour status. The official system may instead show work discontinuation or absent from work. |
| How do I check my status? | Check Qiwa Individuals first for employment status and contract information. Also review Absher and any official SMS notices linked to your Iqama. |
| What is the 60-day period? | In the standard private-sector work-discontinuation process, the worker is given 60 days to complete an eligible transfer or final exit. |
| Can I transfer during the 60 days? | An eligible worker may transfer to a new employer. The new employer normally starts the transfer through Qiwa. |
| Can I leave on final exit? | An eligible worker may use the final-exit route during the allowed period if the official conditions are met. |
| What happens after 60 days? | The status may become or remain absent from work, and the standard transfer or final-exit requests may stop being accepted. |
| Can the old employer cancel the private-sector report? | The published private-sector procedural guide describes the submitted work-discontinuation action as non-retractable. Incorrect or malicious cases may need MHRSD review and formal correction. |
| What if the report is false? | Save evidence immediately, report the possible labour violation to MHRSD, and use Friendly Settlement for personal employment claims where needed. |
| Can an old absent-from-work case still be transferred? | MHRSD launched a Qiwa initiative in September 2025 for specified professional workers with absent-from-work status. Check current Qiwa eligibility. |
| Does huroob automatically cancel unpaid salary? | No. Unpaid salary remains a separate employment claim. |
| Does huroob automatically cancel EOSB? | Not automatically. End-of-service benefits depend on how the employment relationship ended and whether Article 80 or another legal rule applies. |
| Is huroob a criminal case? | Not automatically. It is mainly a labour and residency-status issue, although a separate criminal case can exist independently. |
| Is "exited and did not return" the same as huroob? | No. A worker outside Saudi Arabia after an exit-and-re-entry problem can have a different immigration status. |
| Do domestic workers use the same Qiwa rules? | No. Domestic workers normally use Musaned and separate domestic-worker rules. |
| Can an agent guarantee removal? | No. Use official Qiwa, MHRSD, Absher, Musaned and authorised legal channels. |

## [What Does Huroob Mean in Saudi Arabia?](#what-does-huroob-mean-in-saudi-arabia)

South Asian workers often use several words for this problem:

- Huroob
- Absconding
- Runaway report
- Escape report
- Absence report
- Absent case
- "بلاغ هروب"
- "بلاغ تغيب"

These words are not always the exact status shown by the Saudi government system.

For a private-sector worker, you may instead see wording such as:

| Common or Official Wording | What It Usually Means |
|----|----|
| Huroob / absconding | Common expat description, not always the current official system label |
| بلاغ هروب | Common Arabic phrase for an absconding or runaway report |
| بلاغ تغيب | Absence-related report |
| منقطع عن العمل | Work discontinuation status |
| متغيب عن العمل | Absent-from-work status |
| Contract terminated | Employment contract has ended, but you still need to check residency and transfer status |
| Exited and did not return | Separate immigration issue for someone who left Saudi Arabia and did not return on time |

The exact status matters because each route has different options.

Do not tell an agent only, "I have huroob." Open Qiwa, Absher, Musaned where relevant, or the official MHRSD record and save the exact Arabic or English wording.

Our [Qiwa Saudi Arabia guide](/guides/qiwa-saudi-arabia-guide-work-permits-contracts-transfers-complaints) explains how contracts, work permits, transfer requests and employer records connect.

## [What Does "Escape Report of Resident ID Number Has Been Recorded" Mean?](#what-does-escape-report-of-resident-id-number-has-been-recorded-mean)

Some users see English wording such as:

**"Escape report of resident ID number has been recorded."**

This can be a translated or system-generated description of an absence-related report linked to the resident's Iqama or employment record.

Do not make a major decision from that sentence alone.

Check:

1.  The exact status in Qiwa
2.  The employer name
3.  The contract status
4.  The official action date
5.  Whether a 60-day option is still available
6.  Whether Absher shows final-exit or other residency information
7.  Whether you are a private-sector employee or a domestic worker

If the wording is unclear, contact MHRSD through an official support channel and give them your Iqama details and the exact message shown in the system.

## [Is Huroob the Same as a Criminal Case?](#is-huroob-the-same-as-a-criminal-case)

No, not automatically.

An absent-from-work labour status is mainly connected to:

- Employment relationship
- Work permit
- Employer record
- Iqama and residency status
- Transfer eligibility
- Final exit
- Government labour systems

A separate police or criminal case can exist at the same time, but it is a different matter.

Examples of separate cases could include:

- Theft allegation
- Fraud
- Assault
- Forgery
- Court judgment
- Another police complaint

Clearing an employment-status problem does not automatically clear a separate police or court case.

Likewise, do not assume you have a criminal case simply because Qiwa shows work discontinuation or absent from work.

## [When Can an Employer Rely on Absence Under Saudi Labour Law?](#when-can-an-employer-rely-on-absence-under-saudi-labour-law)

Article 80 of the Saudi Labour Law allows an employer to terminate a worker without award, notice or compensation in specified serious cases, provided the worker has an opportunity to state objections.

One of those cases concerns unjustified absence.

The current official law states that this can apply when the worker is absent without a legitimate reason:

- For **more than 30 days during one contractual year**, or
- For **more than 15 consecutive days**

The law also requires written warning before termination for this reason:

- After **20 days of absence** in the first situation
- After **10 consecutive days of absence** in the second situation

This does not mean every absence automatically becomes huroob.

A worker may have a legitimate reason, for example:

- Approved annual leave
- Official sick leave
- Medical emergency
- Employer instruction not to attend
- Employer preventing the worker from entering the workplace
- Documented workplace safety problem
- Official detention
- Another reason that can be supported with evidence

Article 62 of the Labour Law also says that if a worker presents themselves for work or shows readiness to work but cannot work because of a reason attributable to the employer, the worker is entitled to wages for that period.

The practical lesson is simple: **keep evidence**.

## [How the Private-Sector Qiwa Process Works](#how-the-private-sector-qiwa-process-works)

The MHRSD procedural guide explains the standard work-discontinuation process for relevant private-sector cases.

### [Step 1: The Employer Submits the Work-Discontinuation Action](#step-1-the-employer-submits-the-work-discontinuation-action)

The employer or authorised representative uses Qiwa to submit the action when the official conditions are met.

The published guide connects the process to the same main absence thresholds described above.

### [Step 2: The Worker and Employer Are Notified](#step-2-the-worker-and-employer-are-notified)

The worker and employer are notified electronically.

The worker's record is removed from the establishment, and the worker is no longer counted under that employer for Nitaqat.

### [Step 3: The 60-Day Period Starts](#step-3-the-60-day-period-starts)

The worker is given **60 days from the official action date**.

During that period, an eligible worker may have two main options:

1.  Transfer to another employer
2.  Complete final exit

For the standard transfer route in the published guide, transfer eligibility includes the worker having spent more than 12 months in Saudi Arabia.

The live Qiwa result is still what matters for your own case.

### [Step 4: If No Action Is Completed](#step-4-if-no-action-is-completed)

If the worker does not complete an eligible transfer or final exit during the allowed period, the status can become **absent from work** in the connected ministry systems.

The standard transfer and final-exit requests may then stop being accepted through the normal 60-day route.

This is why waiting is dangerous.

## [What the 60-Day Period Really Means](#what-the-60-day-period-really-means)

The 60 days are not a punishment period that you should simply wait out.

They are a limited time to correct the situation.

### [Option 1: Transfer to a New Employer](#option-1-transfer-to-a-new-employer)

If your goal is to stay in Saudi Arabia and keep working, an eligible new employer normally starts the transfer request in Qiwa.

The process may include:

1.  New employer checks your eligibility
2.  New employer creates the transfer request
3.  Employment contract is added
4.  Worker reviews and accepts the request
5.  MHRSD processes the transfer
6.  Connected government records are updated
7.  New employer completes the remaining work-permit and residency steps

Do not accept the sentence "we applied for transfer" as proof that the transfer is finished.

Check the live Qiwa status until the employment relationship is actually moved.

Our [Saudi Iqama transfer guide](/guides/saudi-iqama-transfer-without-current-employer-consent) explains transfer conditions, employer consent issues and common blockers in more detail.

### [Option 2: Final Exit](#option-2-final-exit)

If you want to leave Saudi Arabia permanently, an eligible final-exit route may be available during the allowed period.

Before leaving, check:

- Passport
- Iqama
- Traffic violations
- Family members
- Unpaid salary
- Leave balance
- EOSB position
- Bank account
- Loans
- Vehicle
- Housing
- Mobile and utility accounts
- Final flight

A final exit may solve the residency side, but it does not automatically settle every employment claim.

Use our [Saudi final exit and Iqama cancellation guide](/guides/how-to-cancel-iqama-and-exit-saudi-arabia-properly) before leaving permanently.

## [What Happens After the 60 Days Expire?](#what-happens-after-the-60-days-expire)

Under the standard private-sector procedure, if the worker does not complete a permitted transfer or final exit within the 60-day period, the status can become or remain **absent from work**.

This can create problems such as:

- Normal transfer route no longer accepting the request
- Normal final-exit request no longer accepting the request
- Work permit complications
- Iqama and residency complications
- Inability to work lawfully for another employer
- Need for a special correction route
- Greater risk of enforcement under labour and residency rules
- Difficulty proving a clean end to the old employment relationship

Do not wait until day 55 to start looking for a new employer.

Employer onboarding, Qiwa eligibility, official fees, contract creation and system updates can take time.

## [Can an Old Huroob or Absent-From-Work Status Be Cleared in 2026?](#can-an-old-huroob-or-absent-from-work-status-be-cleared-in-2026)

Possibly, depending on the record.

MHRSD launched a Qiwa initiative starting from **18 September 2025** to regularise the status of specified professional workers recorded as absent from work.

The ministry said the initiative includes several groups, such as:

- Workers whose status became absent from work after the normal 60-day period
- Workers whose status changed after expiry or termination of a documented employment contract
- Expatriate workers with older absence reports from before the work-discontinuation initiative

MHRSD also listed important conditions, including:

- The worker must have completed at least **12 continuous months in Saudi Arabia** before the work discontinuation or contract expiry
- The new employer must agree to pay outstanding work-permit financial charges connected with the worker

The initiative can allow an eligible worker to transfer legally to a new employer.

### [Important: Do Not Assume You Automatically Qualify](#important-do-not-assume-you-automatically-qualify)

Eligibility may depend on:

- Worker category
- Contract history
- Report or status date
- Time spent in Saudi Arabia
- New employer
- Establishment eligibility
- Work permit
- Outstanding fees
- Connected government records
- Whether the correction option is currently available for your record

Check your live Qiwa account and ask the new employer to check the transfer route before paying anyone.

## [How to Remove Huroob in Saudi Arabia](#how-to-remove-huroob-in-saudi-arabia)

There is no universal "remove huroob" button.

The route depends on what your official record actually says.

### [Situation 1: You Are Still Inside the 60-Day Period](#situation-1-you-are-still-inside-the-60-day-period)

Your practical options may be:

- Complete an eligible transfer to a new employer, or
- Complete final exit

Act before the deadline.

### [Situation 2: The 60 Days Already Passed](#situation-2-the-60-days-already-passed)

Check whether the current Qiwa status-correction initiative is available for your record.

A real new employer should check Qiwa eligibility and confirm:

- Whether transfer is allowed
- What outstanding fees appear
- What contract is required
- What government steps remain

Do not pay a private person to create a fake company transfer.

### [Situation 3: The Report Is False or Malicious](#situation-3-the-report-is-false-or-malicious)

Do not simply search for a paid "huroob removal" service.

Save your evidence and challenge the employer's action through official channels.

### [Situation 4: You Are a Domestic Worker](#situation-4-you-are-a-domestic-worker)

Use Musaned and the domestic-worker rules, not the standard private-sector Qiwa process.

### [Situation 5: You Are Outside Saudi Arabia](#situation-5-you-are-outside-saudi-arabia)

Check whether the problem is actually an exit-and-re-entry or "exited and did not return" status rather than an inside-Kingdom work-discontinuation case.

Our updated [Saudi exit and re-entry visa guide](/guides/saudi-exit-re-entry-visa-rules-fees-validity-common-problems) explains the travel side separately.

## [Can the Employer Cancel the Absence Report?](#can-the-employer-cancel-the-absence-report)

For the standard private-sector process described in the MHRSD procedural guide, the employer's submitted work-discontinuation action is described as **non-retractable** after the worker is removed from the establishment's records.

This is important.

Do not rely on a promise such as:

"Pay me and I will cancel your huroob tonight."

A false, malicious or incorrect case can still be challenged, but the solution may require:

- MHRSD labour-violation report
- Qiwa support
- Friendly Settlement
- Labour court where applicable
- Inspection or official review
- Correction by the relevant authority

A system correction is different from the old employer simply pressing an undo button.

## [What If the Huroob or Absence Report Is False?](#what-if-the-huroob-or-absence-report-is-false)

MHRSD's employer-compliance guidance treats an incorrect absence report as a labour violation where an employer reports a worker as absent while the worker is actually on the job in order to blackmail, harm or pressure the worker.

If you believe the report is false, act quickly.

### ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Evidence for a False Huroob or Absence Report

- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Qiwa contract and current contract-status screenshots
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Iqama and passport copies
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Attendance or fingerprint records
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Worksite access records
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Duty roster or timesheets
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Payslips and bank salary transfers
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Work emails, reports or completed assignments
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Messages with supervisor or HR
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Approved annual-leave record
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Official sick-leave record
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Medical or emergency documents
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Messages showing the employer told you not to attend
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Messages showing you asked to return to work
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Evidence that the workplace was closed or you were prevented from entering
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)GOSI employment record where relevant
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)SMS or screenshot showing the work-discontinuation action
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Threats linking the report to resignation, money, transfer or withdrawal of a complaint
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Names of witnesses who can confirm attendance or employer instructions

Do not create fake attendance records, edit screenshots, or manufacture messages. False evidence can damage your case.

### [Step 1: Save the Exact Status and Date](#step-1-save-the-exact-status-and-date)

Take screenshots from Qiwa and save any official SMS.

Record:

- Employer
- Contract
- Status wording
- Official action date
- Last day actually worked
- Date you discovered the status
- Whether you were on approved leave
- Whether you remained ready to work

The official action date matters because it can control the 60-day period.

### [Step 2: Contact the Employer in Writing](#step-2-contact-the-employer-in-writing)

Keep the message factual.

State that the status is incorrect, give the dates, and ask the employer to explain the official basis for the action.

Avoid threats, insults and emotional arguments.

### [Step 3: Report the Possible Labour Violation](#step-3-report-the-possible-labour-violation)

MHRSD provides a **Reporting Violations of Labor Regulations** service for private-sector labour violations.

The official service is free.

Explain:

- What the system shows
- Why you believe it is incorrect
- When you worked
- What evidence you have
- Whether the employer used the report to pressure you

Save the report reference number.

### [Step 4: File Friendly Settlement for Your Personal Claims](#step-4-file-friendly-settlement-for-your-personal-claims)

A labour-violation report tells MHRSD about possible non-compliance.

It may not by itself recover your personal money claims.

Use Friendly Settlement where you also have disputes involving:

- Unpaid wages
- Leave pay
- Deductions
- Contract compensation
- Unlawful termination
- Forced resignation
- Document withholding
- EOSB where legally due
- Other employment entitlements

MHRSD states that Friendly Settlement is the first stage for labour disputes and that unresolved cases can be referred to labour court.

Our [Saudi labour complaint guide](/guides/file-labour-complaint-saudi-arabia-qiwa-mhrsd) explains the filing process in simple steps.

### [Step 5: Keep Checking the 60-Day Options](#step-5-keep-checking-the-60-day-options)

Do not assume that filing a complaint automatically pauses every Qiwa deadline.

Continue checking whether an eligible transfer or final-exit option remains available while the complaint is being reviewed.

Ask MHRSD what applies to your exact record.

## [Step-by-Step: What to Do Today If You Discover Huroob](#step-by-step-what-to-do-today-if-you-discover-huroob)

### [Step 1: Confirm Whether You Are Inside Saudi Arabia](#step-1-confirm-whether-you-are-inside-saudi-arabia)

The correct route changes depending on whether you are:

- Inside Saudi Arabia
- Outside on exit and re-entry
- Outside after the return visa expired
- Already on final exit
- Detained
- A domestic worker

Do not use an inside-Kingdom transfer plan for an outside-Kingdom immigration problem.

### [Step 2: Open Qiwa Individuals](#step-2-open-qiwa-individuals)

Check:

- Employer name
- Contract status
- Work-discontinuation status
- Absent-from-work status
- Official action date
- Transfer option
- Pending offers
- Notices
- Work permit information where available

Save screenshots.

### [Step 3: Check Absher](#step-3-check-absher)

Review:

- Iqama status
- Passport details
- Final-exit information where available
- Exit and re-entry record
- Other residency or travel information

Qiwa is mainly important for the labour relationship. Absher is important for personal residency and travel services.

### [Step 4: Calculate the Deadline](#step-4-calculate-the-deadline)

Count from the **official system date**, not from:

- The day your coworker told you
- The date an agent checked
- Your last salary
- The date you received an old screenshot
- The day you first heard the word huroob

If you cannot identify the official date, ask MHRSD or Qiwa support.

### [Step 5: Decide Your Main Goal](#step-5-decide-your-main-goal)

Choose what you actually want:

- Stay in Saudi Arabia and transfer
- Challenge a false report
- Leave on final exit
- Recover salary and benefits
- Correct an old absent-from-work status

You may need more than one official service, but a clear goal stops you wasting time.

### [Step 6: If Transferring, Find a Genuine Employer](#step-6-if-transferring-find-a-genuine-employer)

Ask the new employer for:

- Legal establishment name
- Written job offer
- Wage
- Profession
- Contract term
- Work location
- Qiwa transfer request
- Clear explanation of official fees and who will pay them

A private person who promises "transfer without a company" is a major warning sign.

### [Step 7: Protect Your Employment Claims](#step-7-protect-your-employment-claims)

Save proof for:

- Unpaid salary
- Annual leave
- Overtime
- Notice pay
- Expenses
- Contract compensation
- Final settlement
- EOSB position

If Article 80 is being used against you, do not assume the EOSB outcome either way. The legal effect depends on whether the Article 80 termination requirements were actually met and on the facts of the case.

Our [Saudi end-of-service benefits guide](/guides/saudi-end-of-service-benefits-calculate-eosb) explains the calculation and the effect of different contract-ending situations.

### [Step 8: Keep a Case Timeline](#step-8-keep-a-case-timeline)

Use a simple table:

| Date | Action | Reference | Result |
|----|----|----|----|
| Day 1 | Checked Qiwa | Screenshot saved | Status confirmed |
| Day 1 | Contacted HR | Email or message saved | Awaiting response |
| Day 2 | MHRSD violation report | Reference number | Under review |
| Day 3 | New employer checked transfer | Qiwa result | Eligible / not eligible |
| Day 4 | Friendly Settlement filed if needed | Case number | Pending |

Real dates and reference numbers are much more useful than trying to remember everything later.

## [What If You Left Because the Employer Broke the Contract?](#what-if-you-left-because-the-employer-broke-the-contract)

Article 81 of the Saudi Labour Law allows a worker to leave without notice while retaining statutory rights in specified serious situations.

These include certain cases where:

- Employer fails to meet essential contractual or legal obligations
- Employer deceived the worker about employment conditions
- Worker is assigned fundamentally different work without consent contrary to the law
- Employer or responsible person commits assault or serious misconduct
- Employer treatment is harsh, unjust or humiliating
- Workplace presents a serious safety or health danger that the employer knew about and did not correct
- Employer conduct forces the worker to appear responsible for ending the contract

Article 81 is not an automatic online protection against an absence status.

If you leave because of a serious employer breach, keep evidence and use the official complaint process.

Possible evidence includes:

- Unpaid salary records
- Safety complaints
- Medical reports
- Police reports where relevant
- Threats
- Contract mismatch
- Written requests asking the employer to correct the problem
- MHRSD reports
- Witness details

Do not simply disappear and try to explain the reason months later.

## [What If the Employer Has Your Passport?](#what-if-the-employer-has-your-passport)

Passport withholding is a separate employment problem.

If your employer refuses to return your passport, ask for it in writing and keep proof of the request.

A missing passport can make final exit, transfer, travel and case handling more difficult.

Our [Saudi employer holding your passport guide](/guides/saudi-employer-holding-passport-rights-what-to-do) explains the evidence and complaint steps.

## [What If You Are Outside Saudi Arabia?](#what-if-you-are-outside-saudi-arabia)

A worker who left Saudi Arabia on an exit-and-re-entry visa and did not return can have a different immigration status from a worker who stopped attending work inside Saudi Arabia.

Check:

- Exit and re-entry visa status
- Return-before date
- Iqama
- Passport
- Employer record
- Absher
- Muqeem
- Qiwa

Do not tell an agent only that you have huroob. Show the exact official status.

## [Domestic Worker Huroob and Absence Rules](#domestic-worker-huroob-and-absence-rules)

Domestic workers do **not** normally use the standard private-sector Qiwa process.

They use Musaned and separate domestic-worker rules.

This can include:

- Housemaids
- Domestic drivers
- Household nurses
- Private guards
- Gardeners
- Other professions classified under domestic or support labour

### [Employer Withdrawal Period](#employer-withdrawal-period)

The published domestic-worker controls state that, where the conditions apply, the employer may withdraw an absence report within **15 days** from submission. After that, the report becomes final under those controls.

The same published controls state that the employer cannot withdraw a report submitted during the worker's first 90 days after entering Saudi Arabia.

### [If the Contract Is Ended for Work Discontinuation During the First Two Years](#if-the-contract-is-ended-for-work-discontinuation-during-the-first-two-years)

MHRSD's current Musaned guidance says that if the domestic worker's contract is terminated because of work discontinuation during the **first two years after entry to Saudi Arabia**, the worker must complete final exit within **60 days**.

If the worker does not leave within that period, the worker can become non-compliant with residency and labour rules.

### [If the Worker Has Been in Saudi Arabia for More Than Two Years](#if-the-worker-has-been-in-saudi-arabia-for-more-than-two-years)

If the domestic worker's contract is ended because of work discontinuation **after two years from entry**, the worker must normally either:

- Complete final exit, or
- Transfer to a new employer

within **60 days** from the work-discontinuation date.

If the worker does neither, the worker can become absent from work and non-compliant with the applicable rules.

### [Old Domestic-Worker Correction Initiative](#old-domestic-worker-correction-initiative)

MHRSD announced a separate correction window for older absent domestic workers and extended it from November 2025 for six months.

Do **not** assume that temporary correction window is still open in September 2026.

Check the current Musaned screen and MHRSD announcement before relying on any old article, video or social-media post.

## [Can an Agent Clear Huroob?](#can-an-agent-clear-huroob)

No private agent can lawfully guarantee the outcome of a government status.

Be careful if someone promises:

- "Huroob removal in one hour"
- Transfer without a genuine employer
- Fake Qiwa contract
- Backdated attendance
- Guaranteed MHRSD decision
- Guaranteed final exit
- Government cancellation for cash paid to a personal account
- "Inside contact" who needs your Absher or Nafath verification code

Use only:

- Qiwa
- MHRSD
- Absher
- Musaned for domestic workers
- Genuine employer representatives
- Licensed lawyers where legal representation is actually needed

Never share:

- Absher password
- Nafath approval
- Qiwa login
- Bank OTP
- Email verification code

## [Fees and Processing Time](#fees-and-processing-time)

| Action | Fee Guidance | Timing Guidance |
|----|----|----|
| Checking Qiwa or Absher | Do not pay an agent just to check your own official account | Normally available after login if the record is accessible |
| MHRSD labour-violation report | Official service is free | MHRSD lists a 3-day service level, but actual status correction or investigation can take longer |
| Friendly Settlement | Official service is free | MHRSD lists a settlement stage of up to 21 working days before unresolved cases can be referred onward |
| Employee transfer | Government or work-permit related charges may apply | Depends on worker eligibility, new employer, outstanding fees and connected systems |
| 2025 professional-worker correction initiative | New employer may need to pay outstanding work-permit financial charges | Depends on live Qiwa eligibility and completion by the new employer |
| Final exit | Check the live official route | Depends on immigration, passport, Iqama, violations and current status |
| Private legal help | Private provider fees vary | Get the scope and fee in writing before paying |

Do not pay an agent to "open the 60 days" or create a fake transfer.

## [Common Problems](#common-problems)

### [I Did Not Receive an SMS](#i-did-not-receive-an-sms)

Do not assume there is no case.

Check Qiwa directly. An old mobile number, network issue or missed message can prevent you seeing the SMS.

### [I Do Not Know the Official Report Date](#i-do-not-know-the-official-report-date)

Ask MHRSD or Qiwa support to confirm the official action date.

Do not calculate the 60-day period from rumours or memory.

### [A New Employer Says Transfer Is Impossible](#a-new-employer-says-transfer-is-impossible)

Ask the employer to show you the actual Qiwa eligibility result.

Possible blockers include:

- Worker category
- Less than the required time in Saudi Arabia for the relevant route
- Old report date
- Work permit
- Outstanding fees
- New establishment eligibility
- Pending request
- Contract issue
- Another government status

### [The Old Employer Wants Money](#the-old-employer-wants-money)

Do not pay a manager or private person merely because they say they can change the government status.

An employer may have a genuine legal or contractual claim in some cases, but that is different from demanding unofficial cash for a government correction.

Use documented official payment routes and written legal claims.

### [I Have Unpaid Salary](#i-have-unpaid-salary)

File the appropriate employment claim.

Status correction and wage recovery are separate problems.

### [My Iqama Is Expired](#my-iqama-is-expired)

An expired Iqama can make the case more complicated.

Check:

- Qiwa transfer eligibility
- Current professional-worker correction initiative
- Work-permit status
- New employer requirements
- MHRSD guidance

Do not assume Iqama expiry automatically creates huroob. Check the actual official status.

### [The 60 Days Already Passed](#the-60-days-already-passed)

Check whether the September 2025 professional-worker status-correction initiative is available in your Qiwa record.

Ask a genuine new employer to check the transfer route.

### [The Employer Says a False Report Cannot Be Challenged](#the-employer-says-a-false-report-cannot-be-challenged)

The standard private-sector action may be described as non-retractable by the employer, but an incorrect or malicious report can still be reported and reviewed through official channels.

These are two different things.

## [Common Mistakes to Avoid](#common-mistakes-to-avoid)

### ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Mistakes That Can Make a Huroob Case Worse

- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Ignoring the first Qiwa or SMS notice
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Waiting until the last days of the 60-day period
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Using the word huroob without checking the exact official status
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Paying an unofficial agent for guaranteed removal
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Accepting a fake employer transfer
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Working for a new employer before the legal transfer is complete
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Deleting attendance, salary or message evidence
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Stopping work without keeping evidence of the reason
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Assuming a complaint automatically pauses the 60-day period
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Assuming the old employer can always cancel a private-sector report
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Confusing absent from work with exited and did not return
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Using Qiwa private-sector rules for a domestic worker
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Signing a false resignation or settlement
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Giving up genuine salary claims because someone promises a status change
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Assuming EOSB is always payable or always lost without checking how the contract legally ended
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Sharing Absher, Nafath, Qiwa, bank or email verification codes
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Relying on an expired temporary correction initiative without checking the current portal

## [Official Support Channels](#official-support-channels)

Use the channel that matches your problem.

- **Qiwa:** employment contract, private-sector work status, transfer and professional-worker correction
- **MHRSD:** labour guidance, violation reports and employment complaints
- **MHRSD phone:** 19911
- **Friendly Settlement:** salary, termination, compensation and other personal labour disputes
- **Absher:** personal residency, visa and travel services
- **Musaned:** domestic-worker contracts, mobility and absence matters
- **Police or emergency services:** violence, confinement, threats or a separate criminal matter

Keep every reference number.

## [Official Sources Checked](#official-sources-checked)

This guide was reviewed against official Saudi government sources on **September 7, 2026**.

- [MHRSD Employer Compliance Guide on incorrect absence reports](https://www.hrsd.gov.sa/sites/default/files/2023-02/E14102020.pdf)
- [MHRSD Reporting Violations of Labor Regulations](https://www.hrsd.gov.sa/en/ministry-services/services/%D8%B1%D8%B5%D8%AF-%D8%A8%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%BA%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D9%85%D8%AE%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%81%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D9%86%D8%B8%D8%A7%D9%85-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D9%85%D9%84)

- [Qiwa official platform](https://www.qiwa.sa/)
- [Absher official platform](https://www.absher.sa/)

Requirements and portal options can change. Check the live official system before paying, transferring, leaving Saudi Arabia or assuming a case has been cleared.

## Frequently Asked Questions

What is huroob in Saudi Arabia?![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Huroob is the common expat name for an absence or absconding-related labour status. Saudi official systems now commonly use wording such as work discontinuation or absent from work. Always check the exact status in Qiwa or the relevant official system.

What does 'escape report of resident ID number has been recorded' mean?![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

It usually indicates that an absence-related report or status has been recorded against the resident's Iqama or employment record. The English wording can be a translated system phrase, so check Qiwa, the official action date and your exact status before deciding what to do.

How do I check if I have huroob or absent-from-work status?![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Open Qiwa Individuals and check your employer, contract and employment status. Save any work-discontinuation or absent-from-work message and the official date. Also check Absher for connected residency and visa information.

How many days do I have after work discontinuation?![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The standard private-sector procedure gives a 60-day period from the official work-discontinuation action date for an eligible worker to complete a transfer or final exit.

Can I transfer to another employer during the 60 days?![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

An eligible worker may be able to transfer. The new employer normally starts the request in Qiwa, adds the employment contract and completes the connected government process. Live Qiwa eligibility controls the result.

Can I get final exit during the 60-day period?![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The standard procedure provides a final-exit option for eligible workers during the allowed period. Check the live Qiwa and Absher record, passport, Iqama and any unresolved violations before relying on it.

What happens when the 60 days expire?![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The status can become or remain absent from work, and the normal transfer and final-exit requests may stop being accepted. Some professional workers may qualify for the status-correction initiative launched by MHRSD in September 2025.

How can I remove huroob in Saudi Arabia?![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

There is no universal one-click removal. If you are inside the 60-day period, an eligible transfer or final exit may solve the status. Older professional-worker cases may qualify for the Qiwa correction initiative. False reports should be challenged through MHRSD and the appropriate labour-dispute route. Domestic workers use Musaned.

Can my employer cancel a private-sector absence report?![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The published private-sector procedural guide describes the standard submitted work-discontinuation action as non-retractable by the employer after submission. A false or incorrect case can still be reported, disputed and formally reviewed through MHRSD or other competent channels.

What should I do if the employer filed a false huroob report?![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Save attendance, salary, Qiwa, leave, medical and message evidence immediately. Report the possible labour violation to MHRSD. If you also have personal claims such as unpaid wages or unlawful termination, use Friendly Settlement. Do not assume the complaint pauses the 60-day system period.

Can I clear an old absent-from-work status through Qiwa?![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

MHRSD launched a Qiwa initiative in September 2025 for specified professional workers with absent-from-work status. Important conditions include at least 12 continuous months in Saudi Arabia before the relevant event and the new employer agreeing to pay outstanding work-permit financial charges. Check live Qiwa eligibility.

Does huroob mean I lose all unpaid salary?![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

No. Unpaid salary is a separate employment claim. Keep wage records and use the official labour-dispute route if the employer does not pay what is legally due.

Does huroob mean I automatically lose end-of-service benefits?![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

No single answer applies to every case. EOSB can depend on how the contract legally ended. If an employer validly terminates under Article 80, the award can be affected. If Article 80 does not legally apply, the result may be different. Keep evidence and use the official dispute route where needed.

Can I work for another company before the transfer is completed?![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Do not start unauthorised work. The new employment relationship and required work authorisation should be completed through the official transfer process first.

Is absent from work the same as exited and did not return?![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

No. Absent from work is mainly an employment-status issue. Exited and did not return concerns a worker who is outside Saudi Arabia after an exit-and-re-entry problem and is handled through different immigration records.

Do domestic workers follow the same huroob rules?![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

No. Domestic workers normally use Musaned and separate rules. Published controls include a 15-day employer withdrawal period in qualifying cases. Current MHRSD guidance also distinguishes workers whose contracts end for work discontinuation during the first two years after entry from workers who have been in Saudi Arabia for more than two years.

Can an agent guarantee huroob removal?![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

No legitimate agent can guarantee a government decision. Use Qiwa, MHRSD, Absher, Musaned and authorised legal channels. Never pay for a fake transfer or share your Absher, Nafath, Qiwa or bank verification codes.

## [Bottom Line](#bottom-line)

A Saudi huroob or absconding case is not one simple status with one simple solution.

Start by checking the **exact official status and date**.

For many standard private-sector work-discontinuation cases, the worker has **60 days** to complete an eligible transfer to a new employer or final exit. If no action is completed, the status can become absent from work and the normal route can become much harder.

If the report is false, collect evidence and use the official MHRSD violation and labour-dispute channels immediately.

If the 60-day period has already passed, check whether the September 2025 professional-worker Qiwa correction initiative is available for your record.

If you are a domestic worker, use Musaned and the domestic-worker rules.

Do not pay an unofficial person for guaranteed huroob removal. The safest path is the one shown by Qiwa, MHRSD, Absher or Musaned for your exact case.

# Saudi Huroob (Absconding) 2026: Check, Remove or Transfer

Saudi huroob and absconding guide for 2026. Check absent-from-work status, understand the 60-day Qiwa period, transfer or final exit options, false reports and domestic worker rules.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

GulfVisaHub Editorial Team

August 10, 2026 · 31 min read

Share:[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)X](https://x.com/intent/tweet?text=Saudi%20Huroob%20(Absconding)%202026%3A%20Check%2C%20Remove%20or%20Transfer&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.gulfvisahub.org%2Fguides%2Fsaudi-absconding-case-what-it-means-how-to-clear&via=GulfVisaHub)[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.gulfvisahub.org%2Fguides%2Fsaudi-absconding-case-what-it-means-how-to-clear)[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Email](mailto:?subject=Saudi%20Huroob%20(Absconding)%202026%3A%20Check%2C%20Remove%20or%20Transfer&body=Saudi%20Huroob%20(Absconding)%202026%3A%20Check%2C%20Remove%20or%20Transfer%0A%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.gulfvisahub.org%2Fguides%2Fsaudi-absconding-case-what-it-means-how-to-clear)

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Copy link

[Editorial policy](/editorial-policy)

In everyday expat language, **huroob** or an **absconding case** usually means that a worker has an absence-related status in Saudi labour or residency records. Saudi official systems now more commonly use terms such as **work discontinuation** and **absent from work**.

For many private-sector Qiwa cases, the important period is **60 days**. During that period, an eligible worker may be able to transfer legally to a new employer or complete final exit. If no permitted action is completed, the status can become **absent from work**, and the normal transfer or final-exit route can become harder.

There is no single button that removes every huroob case. The correct solution depends on the exact Qiwa status, report or action date, contract history, whether the worker is inside Saudi Arabia, whether the case is false, and whether a current status-correction route is available.

## [Quick Answer](#quick-answer)

| Question | Practical Answer |
|----|----|
| What is huroob in Saudi Arabia? | Huroob is a common expat word for an absence or absconding-related labour status. The official system may instead show work discontinuation or absent from work. |
| How do I check my status? | Check Qiwa Individuals first for employment status and contract information. Also review Absher and any official SMS notices linked to your Iqama. |
| What is the 60-day period? | In the standard private-sector work-discontinuation process, the worker is given 60 days to complete an eligible transfer or final exit. |
| Can I transfer during the 60 days? | An eligible worker may transfer to a new employer. The new employer normally starts the transfer through Qiwa. |
| Can I leave on final exit? | An eligible worker may use the final-exit route during the allowed period if the official conditions are met. |
| What happens after 60 days? | The status may become or remain absent from work, and the standard transfer or final-exit requests may stop being accepted. |
| Can the old employer cancel the private-sector report? | The published private-sector procedural guide describes the submitted work-discontinuation action as non-retractable. Incorrect or malicious cases may need MHRSD review and formal correction. |
| What if the report is false? | Save evidence immediately, report the possible labour violation to MHRSD, and use Friendly Settlement for personal employment claims where needed. |
| Can an old absent-from-work case still be transferred? | MHRSD launched a Qiwa initiative in September 2025 for specified professional workers with absent-from-work status. Check current Qiwa eligibility. |
| Does huroob automatically cancel unpaid salary? | No. Unpaid salary remains a separate employment claim. |
| Does huroob automatically cancel EOSB? | Not automatically. End-of-service benefits depend on how the employment relationship ended and whether Article 80 or another legal rule applies. |
| Is huroob a criminal case? | Not automatically. It is mainly a labour and residency-status issue, although a separate criminal case can exist independently. |
| Is "exited and did not return" the same as huroob? | No. A worker outside Saudi Arabia after an exit-and-re-entry problem can have a different immigration status. |
| Do domestic workers use the same Qiwa rules? | No. Domestic workers normally use Musaned and separate domestic-worker rules. |
| Can an agent guarantee removal? | No. Use official Qiwa, MHRSD, Absher, Musaned and authorised legal channels. |

## [What Does Huroob Mean in Saudi Arabia?](#what-does-huroob-mean-in-saudi-arabia)

South Asian workers often use several words for this problem:

- Huroob
- Absconding
- Runaway report
- Escape report
- Absence report
- Absent case
- "بلاغ هروب"
- "بلاغ تغيب"

These words are not always the exact status shown by the Saudi government system.

For a private-sector worker, you may instead see wording such as:

| Common or Official Wording | What It Usually Means |
|----|----|
| Huroob / absconding | Common expat description, not always the current official system label |
| بلاغ هروب | Common Arabic phrase for an absconding or runaway report |
| بلاغ تغيب | Absence-related report |
| منقطع عن العمل | Work discontinuation status |
| متغيب عن العمل | Absent-from-work status |
| Contract terminated | Employment contract has ended, but you still need to check residency and transfer status |
| Exited and did not return | Separate immigration issue for someone who left Saudi Arabia and did not return on time |

The exact status matters because each route has different options.

Do not tell an agent only, "I have huroob." Open Qiwa, Absher, Musaned where relevant, or the official MHRSD record and save the exact Arabic or English wording.

Our [Qiwa Saudi Arabia guide](/guides/qiwa-saudi-arabia-guide-work-permits-contracts-transfers-complaints) explains how contracts, work permits, transfer requests and employer records connect.

## [What Does "Escape Report of Resident ID Number Has Been Recorded" Mean?](#what-does-escape-report-of-resident-id-number-has-been-recorded-mean)

Some users see English wording such as:

**"Escape report of resident ID number has been recorded."**

This can be a translated or system-generated description of an absence-related report linked to the resident's Iqama or employment record.

Do not make a major decision from that sentence alone.

Check:

1.  The exact status in Qiwa
2.  The employer name
3.  The contract status
4.  The official action date
5.  Whether a 60-day option is still available
6.  Whether Absher shows final-exit or other residency information
7.  Whether you are a private-sector employee or a domestic worker

If the wording is unclear, contact MHRSD through an official support channel and give them your Iqama details and the exact message shown in the system.

## [Is Huroob the Same as a Criminal Case?](#is-huroob-the-same-as-a-criminal-case)

No, not automatically.

An absent-from-work labour status is mainly connected to:

- Employment relationship
- Work permit
- Employer record
- Iqama and residency status
- Transfer eligibility
- Final exit
- Government labour systems

A separate police or criminal case can exist at the same time, but it is a different matter.

Examples of separate cases could include:

- Theft allegation
- Fraud
- Assault
- Forgery
- Court judgment
- Another police complaint

Clearing an employment-status problem does not automatically clear a separate police or court case.

Likewise, do not assume you have a criminal case simply because Qiwa shows work discontinuation or absent from work.

## [When Can an Employer Rely on Absence Under Saudi Labour Law?](#when-can-an-employer-rely-on-absence-under-saudi-labour-law)

Article 80 of the Saudi Labour Law allows an employer to terminate a worker without award, notice or compensation in specified serious cases, provided the worker has an opportunity to state objections.

One of those cases concerns unjustified absence.

The current official law states that this can apply when the worker is absent without a legitimate reason:

- For **more than 30 days during one contractual year**, or
- For **more than 15 consecutive days**

The law also requires written warning before termination for this reason:

- After **20 days of absence** in the first situation
- After **10 consecutive days of absence** in the second situation

This does not mean every absence automatically becomes huroob.

A worker may have a legitimate reason, for example:

- Approved annual leave
- Official sick leave
- Medical emergency
- Employer instruction not to attend
- Employer preventing the worker from entering the workplace
- Documented workplace safety problem
- Official detention
- Another reason that can be supported with evidence

Article 62 of the Labour Law also says that if a worker presents themselves for work or shows readiness to work but cannot work because of a reason attributable to the employer, the worker is entitled to wages for that period.

The practical lesson is simple: **keep evidence**.

## [How the Private-Sector Qiwa Process Works](#how-the-private-sector-qiwa-process-works)

The MHRSD procedural guide explains the standard work-discontinuation process for relevant private-sector cases.

### [Step 1: The Employer Submits the Work-Discontinuation Action](#step-1-the-employer-submits-the-work-discontinuation-action)

The employer or authorised representative uses Qiwa to submit the action when the official conditions are met.

The published guide connects the process to the same main absence thresholds described above.

### [Step 2: The Worker and Employer Are Notified](#step-2-the-worker-and-employer-are-notified)

The worker and employer are notified electronically.

The worker's record is removed from the establishment, and the worker is no longer counted under that employer for Nitaqat.

### [Step 3: The 60-Day Period Starts](#step-3-the-60-day-period-starts)

The worker is given **60 days from the official action date**.

During that period, an eligible worker may have two main options:

1.  Transfer to another employer
2.  Complete final exit

For the standard transfer route in the published guide, transfer eligibility includes the worker having spent more than 12 months in Saudi Arabia.

The live Qiwa result is still what matters for your own case.

### [Step 4: If No Action Is Completed](#step-4-if-no-action-is-completed)

If the worker does not complete an eligible transfer or final exit during the allowed period, the status can become **absent from work** in the connected ministry systems.

The standard transfer and final-exit requests may then stop being accepted through the normal 60-day route.

This is why waiting is dangerous.

## [What the 60-Day Period Really Means](#what-the-60-day-period-really-means)

The 60 days are not a punishment period that you should simply wait out.

They are a limited time to correct the situation.

### [Option 1: Transfer to a New Employer](#option-1-transfer-to-a-new-employer)

If your goal is to stay in Saudi Arabia and keep working, an eligible new employer normally starts the transfer request in Qiwa.

The process may include:

1.  New employer checks your eligibility
2.  New employer creates the transfer request
3.  Employment contract is added
4.  Worker reviews and accepts the request
5.  MHRSD processes the transfer
6.  Connected government records are updated
7.  New employer completes the remaining work-permit and residency steps

Do not accept the sentence "we applied for transfer" as proof that the transfer is finished.

Check the live Qiwa status until the employment relationship is actually moved.

Our [Saudi Iqama transfer guide](/guides/saudi-iqama-transfer-without-current-employer-consent) explains transfer conditions, employer consent issues and common blockers in more detail.

### [Option 2: Final Exit](#option-2-final-exit)

If you want to leave Saudi Arabia permanently, an eligible final-exit route may be available during the allowed period.

Before leaving, check:

- Passport
- Iqama
- Traffic violations
- Family members
- Unpaid salary
- Leave balance
- EOSB position
- Bank account
- Loans
- Vehicle
- Housing
- Mobile and utility accounts
- Final flight

A final exit may solve the residency side, but it does not automatically settle every employment claim.

Use our [Saudi final exit and Iqama cancellation guide](/guides/how-to-cancel-iqama-and-exit-saudi-arabia-properly) before leaving permanently.

## [What Happens After the 60 Days Expire?](#what-happens-after-the-60-days-expire)

Under the standard private-sector procedure, if the worker does not complete a permitted transfer or final exit within the 60-day period, the status can become or remain **absent from work**.

This can create problems such as:

- Normal transfer route no longer accepting the request
- Normal final-exit request no longer accepting the request
- Work permit complications
- Iqama and residency complications
- Inability to work lawfully for another employer
- Need for a special correction route
- Greater risk of enforcement under labour and residency rules
- Difficulty proving a clean end to the old employment relationship

Do not wait until day 55 to start looking for a new employer.

Employer onboarding, Qiwa eligibility, official fees, contract creation and system updates can take time.

## [Can an Old Huroob or Absent-From-Work Status Be Cleared in 2026?](#can-an-old-huroob-or-absent-from-work-status-be-cleared-in-2026)

Possibly, depending on the record.

MHRSD launched a Qiwa initiative starting from **18 September 2025** to regularise the status of specified professional workers recorded as absent from work.

The ministry said the initiative includes several groups, such as:

- Workers whose status became absent from work after the normal 60-day period
- Workers whose status changed after expiry or termination of a documented employment contract
- Expatriate workers with older absence reports from before the work-discontinuation initiative

MHRSD also listed important conditions, including:

- The worker must have completed at least **12 continuous months in Saudi Arabia** before the work discontinuation or contract expiry
- The new employer must agree to pay outstanding work-permit financial charges connected with the worker

The initiative can allow an eligible worker to transfer legally to a new employer.

### [Important: Do Not Assume You Automatically Qualify](#important-do-not-assume-you-automatically-qualify)

Eligibility may depend on:

- Worker category
- Contract history
- Report or status date
- Time spent in Saudi Arabia
- New employer
- Establishment eligibility
- Work permit
- Outstanding fees
- Connected government records
- Whether the correction option is currently available for your record

Check your live Qiwa account and ask the new employer to check the transfer route before paying anyone.

## [How to Remove Huroob in Saudi Arabia](#how-to-remove-huroob-in-saudi-arabia)

There is no universal "remove huroob" button.

The route depends on what your official record actually says.

### [Situation 1: You Are Still Inside the 60-Day Period](#situation-1-you-are-still-inside-the-60-day-period)

Your practical options may be:

- Complete an eligible transfer to a new employer, or
- Complete final exit

Act before the deadline.

### [Situation 2: The 60 Days Already Passed](#situation-2-the-60-days-already-passed)

Check whether the current Qiwa status-correction initiative is available for your record.

A real new employer should check Qiwa eligibility and confirm:

- Whether transfer is allowed
- What outstanding fees appear
- What contract is required
- What government steps remain

Do not pay a private person to create a fake company transfer.

### [Situation 3: The Report Is False or Malicious](#situation-3-the-report-is-false-or-malicious)

Do not simply search for a paid "huroob removal" service.

Save your evidence and challenge the employer's action through official channels.

### [Situation 4: You Are a Domestic Worker](#situation-4-you-are-a-domestic-worker)

Use Musaned and the domestic-worker rules, not the standard private-sector Qiwa process.

### [Situation 5: You Are Outside Saudi Arabia](#situation-5-you-are-outside-saudi-arabia)

Check whether the problem is actually an exit-and-re-entry or "exited and did not return" status rather than an inside-Kingdom work-discontinuation case.

Our updated [Saudi exit and re-entry visa guide](/guides/saudi-exit-re-entry-visa-rules-fees-validity-common-problems) explains the travel side separately.

## [Can the Employer Cancel the Absence Report?](#can-the-employer-cancel-the-absence-report)

For the standard private-sector process described in the MHRSD procedural guide, the employer's submitted work-discontinuation action is described as **non-retractable** after the worker is removed from the establishment's records.

This is important.

Do not rely on a promise such as:

"Pay me and I will cancel your huroob tonight."

A false, malicious or incorrect case can still be challenged, but the solution may require:

- MHRSD labour-violation report
- Qiwa support
- Friendly Settlement
- Labour court where applicable
- Inspection or official review
- Correction by the relevant authority

A system correction is different from the old employer simply pressing an undo button.

## [What If the Huroob or Absence Report Is False?](#what-if-the-huroob-or-absence-report-is-false)

MHRSD's employer-compliance guidance treats an incorrect absence report as a labour violation where an employer reports a worker as absent while the worker is actually on the job in order to blackmail, harm or pressure the worker.

If you believe the report is false, act quickly.

### ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Evidence for a False Huroob or Absence Report

- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Qiwa contract and current contract-status screenshots
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Iqama and passport copies
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Attendance or fingerprint records
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Worksite access records
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Duty roster or timesheets
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Payslips and bank salary transfers
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Work emails, reports or completed assignments
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Messages with supervisor or HR
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Approved annual-leave record
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Official sick-leave record
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Medical or emergency documents
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Messages showing the employer told you not to attend
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Messages showing you asked to return to work
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Evidence that the workplace was closed or you were prevented from entering
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)GOSI employment record where relevant
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)SMS or screenshot showing the work-discontinuation action
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Threats linking the report to resignation, money, transfer or withdrawal of a complaint
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Names of witnesses who can confirm attendance or employer instructions

Do not create fake attendance records, edit screenshots, or manufacture messages. False evidence can damage your case.

### [Step 1: Save the Exact Status and Date](#step-1-save-the-exact-status-and-date)

Take screenshots from Qiwa and save any official SMS.

Record:

- Employer
- Contract
- Status wording
- Official action date
- Last day actually worked
- Date you discovered the status
- Whether you were on approved leave
- Whether you remained ready to work

The official action date matters because it can control the 60-day period.

### [Step 2: Contact the Employer in Writing](#step-2-contact-the-employer-in-writing)

Keep the message factual.

State that the status is incorrect, give the dates, and ask the employer to explain the official basis for the action.

Avoid threats, insults and emotional arguments.

### [Step 3: Report the Possible Labour Violation](#step-3-report-the-possible-labour-violation)

MHRSD provides a **Reporting Violations of Labor Regulations** service for private-sector labour violations.

The official service is free.

Explain:

- What the system shows
- Why you believe it is incorrect
- When you worked
- What evidence you have
- Whether the employer used the report to pressure you

Save the report reference number.

### [Step 4: File Friendly Settlement for Your Personal Claims](#step-4-file-friendly-settlement-for-your-personal-claims)

A labour-violation report tells MHRSD about possible non-compliance.

It may not by itself recover your personal money claims.

Use Friendly Settlement where you also have disputes involving:

- Unpaid wages
- Leave pay
- Deductions
- Contract compensation
- Unlawful termination
- Forced resignation
- Document withholding
- EOSB where legally due
- Other employment entitlements

MHRSD states that Friendly Settlement is the first stage for labour disputes and that unresolved cases can be referred to labour court.

Our [Saudi labour complaint guide](/guides/file-labour-complaint-saudi-arabia-qiwa-mhrsd) explains the filing process in simple steps.

### [Step 5: Keep Checking the 60-Day Options](#step-5-keep-checking-the-60-day-options)

Do not assume that filing a complaint automatically pauses every Qiwa deadline.

Continue checking whether an eligible transfer or final-exit option remains available while the complaint is being reviewed.

Ask MHRSD what applies to your exact record.

## [Step-by-Step: What to Do Today If You Discover Huroob](#step-by-step-what-to-do-today-if-you-discover-huroob)

### [Step 1: Confirm Whether You Are Inside Saudi Arabia](#step-1-confirm-whether-you-are-inside-saudi-arabia)

The correct route changes depending on whether you are:

- Inside Saudi Arabia
- Outside on exit and re-entry
- Outside after the return visa expired
- Already on final exit
- Detained
- A domestic worker

Do not use an inside-Kingdom transfer plan for an outside-Kingdom immigration problem.

### [Step 2: Open Qiwa Individuals](#step-2-open-qiwa-individuals)

Check:

- Employer name
- Contract status
- Work-discontinuation status
- Absent-from-work status
- Official action date
- Transfer option
- Pending offers
- Notices
- Work permit information where available

Save screenshots.

### [Step 3: Check Absher](#step-3-check-absher)

Review:

- Iqama status
- Passport details
- Final-exit information where available
- Exit and re-entry record
- Other residency or travel information

Qiwa is mainly important for the labour relationship. Absher is important for personal residency and travel services.

### [Step 4: Calculate the Deadline](#step-4-calculate-the-deadline)

Count from the **official system date**, not from:

- The day your coworker told you
- The date an agent checked
- Your last salary
- The date you received an old screenshot
- The day you first heard the word huroob

If you cannot identify the official date, ask MHRSD or Qiwa support.

### [Step 5: Decide Your Main Goal](#step-5-decide-your-main-goal)

Choose what you actually want:

- Stay in Saudi Arabia and transfer
- Challenge a false report
- Leave on final exit
- Recover salary and benefits
- Correct an old absent-from-work status

You may need more than one official service, but a clear goal stops you wasting time.

### [Step 6: If Transferring, Find a Genuine Employer](#step-6-if-transferring-find-a-genuine-employer)

Ask the new employer for:

- Legal establishment name
- Written job offer
- Wage
- Profession
- Contract term
- Work location
- Qiwa transfer request
- Clear explanation of official fees and who will pay them

A private person who promises "transfer without a company" is a major warning sign.

### [Step 7: Protect Your Employment Claims](#step-7-protect-your-employment-claims)

Save proof for:

- Unpaid salary
- Annual leave
- Overtime
- Notice pay
- Expenses
- Contract compensation
- Final settlement
- EOSB position

If Article 80 is being used against you, do not assume the EOSB outcome either way. The legal effect depends on whether the Article 80 termination requirements were actually met and on the facts of the case.

Our [Saudi end-of-service benefits guide](/guides/saudi-end-of-service-benefits-calculate-eosb) explains the calculation and the effect of different contract-ending situations.

### [Step 8: Keep a Case Timeline](#step-8-keep-a-case-timeline)

Use a simple table:

| Date | Action | Reference | Result |
|----|----|----|----|
| Day 1 | Checked Qiwa | Screenshot saved | Status confirmed |
| Day 1 | Contacted HR | Email or message saved | Awaiting response |
| Day 2 | MHRSD violation report | Reference number | Under review |
| Day 3 | New employer checked transfer | Qiwa result | Eligible / not eligible |
| Day 4 | Friendly Settlement filed if needed | Case number | Pending |

Real dates and reference numbers are much more useful than trying to remember everything later.

## [What If You Left Because the Employer Broke the Contract?](#what-if-you-left-because-the-employer-broke-the-contract)

Article 81 of the Saudi Labour Law allows a worker to leave without notice while retaining statutory rights in specified serious situations.

These include certain cases where:

- Employer fails to meet essential contractual or legal obligations
- Employer deceived the worker about employment conditions
- Worker is assigned fundamentally different work without consent contrary to the law
- Employer or responsible person commits assault or serious misconduct
- Employer treatment is harsh, unjust or humiliating
- Workplace presents a serious safety or health danger that the employer knew about and did not correct
- Employer conduct forces the worker to appear responsible for ending the contract

Article 81 is not an automatic online protection against an absence status.

If you leave because of a serious employer breach, keep evidence and use the official complaint process.

Possible evidence includes:

- Unpaid salary records
- Safety complaints
- Medical reports
- Police reports where relevant
- Threats
- Contract mismatch
- Written requests asking the employer to correct the problem
- MHRSD reports
- Witness details

Do not simply disappear and try to explain the reason months later.

## [What If the Employer Has Your Passport?](#what-if-the-employer-has-your-passport)

Passport withholding is a separate employment problem.

If your employer refuses to return your passport, ask for it in writing and keep proof of the request.

A missing passport can make final exit, transfer, travel and case handling more difficult.

Our [Saudi employer holding your passport guide](/guides/saudi-employer-holding-passport-rights-what-to-do) explains the evidence and complaint steps.

## [What If You Are Outside Saudi Arabia?](#what-if-you-are-outside-saudi-arabia)

A worker who left Saudi Arabia on an exit-and-re-entry visa and did not return can have a different immigration status from a worker who stopped attending work inside Saudi Arabia.

Check:

- Exit and re-entry visa status
- Return-before date
- Iqama
- Passport
- Employer record
- Absher
- Muqeem
- Qiwa

Do not tell an agent only that you have huroob. Show the exact official status.

## [Domestic Worker Huroob and Absence Rules](#domestic-worker-huroob-and-absence-rules)

Domestic workers do **not** normally use the standard private-sector Qiwa process.

They use Musaned and separate domestic-worker rules.

This can include:

- Housemaids
- Domestic drivers
- Household nurses
- Private guards
- Gardeners
- Other professions classified under domestic or support labour

### [Employer Withdrawal Period](#employer-withdrawal-period)

The published domestic-worker controls state that, where the conditions apply, the employer may withdraw an absence report within **15 days** from submission. After that, the report becomes final under those controls.

The same published controls state that the employer cannot withdraw a report submitted during the worker's first 90 days after entering Saudi Arabia.

### [If the Contract Is Ended for Work Discontinuation During the First Two Years](#if-the-contract-is-ended-for-work-discontinuation-during-the-first-two-years)

MHRSD's current Musaned guidance says that if the domestic worker's contract is terminated because of work discontinuation during the **first two years after entry to Saudi Arabia**, the worker must complete final exit within **60 days**.

If the worker does not leave within that period, the worker can become non-compliant with residency and labour rules.

### [If the Worker Has Been in Saudi Arabia for More Than Two Years](#if-the-worker-has-been-in-saudi-arabia-for-more-than-two-years)

If the domestic worker's contract is ended because of work discontinuation **after two years from entry**, the worker must normally either:

- Complete final exit, or
- Transfer to a new employer

within **60 days** from the work-discontinuation date.

If the worker does neither, the worker can become absent from work and non-compliant with the applicable rules.

### [Old Domestic-Worker Correction Initiative](#old-domestic-worker-correction-initiative)

MHRSD announced a separate correction window for older absent domestic workers and extended it from November 2025 for six months.

Do **not** assume that temporary correction window is still open in September 2026.

Check the current Musaned screen and MHRSD announcement before relying on any old article, video or social-media post.

## [Can an Agent Clear Huroob?](#can-an-agent-clear-huroob)

No private agent can lawfully guarantee the outcome of a government status.

Be careful if someone promises:

- "Huroob removal in one hour"
- Transfer without a genuine employer
- Fake Qiwa contract
- Backdated attendance
- Guaranteed MHRSD decision
- Guaranteed final exit
- Government cancellation for cash paid to a personal account
- "Inside contact" who needs your Absher or Nafath verification code

Use only:

- Qiwa
- MHRSD
- Absher
- Musaned for domestic workers
- Genuine employer representatives
- Licensed lawyers where legal representation is actually needed

Never share:

- Absher password
- Nafath approval
- Qiwa login
- Bank OTP
- Email verification code

## [Fees and Processing Time](#fees-and-processing-time)

| Action | Fee Guidance | Timing Guidance |
|----|----|----|
| Checking Qiwa or Absher | Do not pay an agent just to check your own official account | Normally available after login if the record is accessible |
| MHRSD labour-violation report | Official service is free | MHRSD lists a 3-day service level, but actual status correction or investigation can take longer |
| Friendly Settlement | Official service is free | MHRSD lists a settlement stage of up to 21 working days before unresolved cases can be referred onward |
| Employee transfer | Government or work-permit related charges may apply | Depends on worker eligibility, new employer, outstanding fees and connected systems |
| 2025 professional-worker correction initiative | New employer may need to pay outstanding work-permit financial charges | Depends on live Qiwa eligibility and completion by the new employer |
| Final exit | Check the live official route | Depends on immigration, passport, Iqama, violations and current status |
| Private legal help | Private provider fees vary | Get the scope and fee in writing before paying |

Do not pay an agent to "open the 60 days" or create a fake transfer.

## [Common Problems](#common-problems)

### [I Did Not Receive an SMS](#i-did-not-receive-an-sms)

Do not assume there is no case.

Check Qiwa directly. An old mobile number, network issue or missed message can prevent you seeing the SMS.

### [I Do Not Know the Official Report Date](#i-do-not-know-the-official-report-date)

Ask MHRSD or Qiwa support to confirm the official action date.

Do not calculate the 60-day period from rumours or memory.

### [A New Employer Says Transfer Is Impossible](#a-new-employer-says-transfer-is-impossible)

Ask the employer to show you the actual Qiwa eligibility result.

Possible blockers include:

- Worker category
- Less than the required time in Saudi Arabia for the relevant route
- Old report date
- Work permit
- Outstanding fees
- New establishment eligibility
- Pending request
- Contract issue
- Another government status

### [The Old Employer Wants Money](#the-old-employer-wants-money)

Do not pay a manager or private person merely because they say they can change the government status.

An employer may have a genuine legal or contractual claim in some cases, but that is different from demanding unofficial cash for a government correction.

Use documented official payment routes and written legal claims.

### [I Have Unpaid Salary](#i-have-unpaid-salary)

File the appropriate employment claim.

Status correction and wage recovery are separate problems.

### [My Iqama Is Expired](#my-iqama-is-expired)

An expired Iqama can make the case more complicated.

Check:

- Qiwa transfer eligibility
- Current professional-worker correction initiative
- Work-permit status
- New employer requirements
- MHRSD guidance

Do not assume Iqama expiry automatically creates huroob. Check the actual official status.

### [The 60 Days Already Passed](#the-60-days-already-passed)

Check whether the September 2025 professional-worker status-correction initiative is available in your Qiwa record.

Ask a genuine new employer to check the transfer route.

### [The Employer Says a False Report Cannot Be Challenged](#the-employer-says-a-false-report-cannot-be-challenged)

The standard private-sector action may be described as non-retractable by the employer, but an incorrect or malicious report can still be reported and reviewed through official channels.

These are two different things.

## [Common Mistakes to Avoid](#common-mistakes-to-avoid)

- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Waiting until the last days of the 60-day period
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Using the word huroob without checking the exact official status

- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Accepting a fake employer transfer

- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Stopping work without keeping evidence of the reason
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Assuming a complaint automatically pauses the 60-day period
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Assuming the old employer can always cancel a private-sector report
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Confusing absent from work with exited and did not return
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Using Qiwa private-sector rules for a domestic worker

- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Assuming EOSB is always payable or always lost without checking how the contract legally ended
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Sharing Absher, Nafath, Qiwa, bank or email verification codes
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)Relying on an expired temporary correction initiative without checking the current portal

## [Official Support Channels](#official-support-channels)

Use the channel that matches your problem.

- **Qiwa:** employment contract, private-sector work status, transfer and professional-worker correction
- **MHRSD:** labour guidance, violation reports and employment complaints
- **MHRSD phone:** 19911
- **Friendly Settlement:** salary, termination, compensation and other personal labour disputes
- **Absher:** personal residency, visa and travel services
- **Musaned:** domestic-worker contracts, mobility and absence matters
- **Police or emergency services:** violence, confinement, threats or a separate criminal matter

Keep every reference number.
